# AgenEditor — Product & Technical Specification

**Version:** 1.0 — architecture baseline  
**Date:** 2026-11-10  
**Product:** Local-first desktop AI video editor with MCP integration  
**Primary platform:** Windows x64; macOS/Linux later  
**AI control:** External Codex / Claude Code-compatible MCP hosts  
**Product rule:** AgenEditor edits approved media and never generates synthetic footage, imagery, speech or music itself. Storyboards and B-roll may be generated by *external* tools the user runs; they enter the project only as imported, labelled assets (§3.1).

> **Status:** Design specification, not a claim of working software. Architecture decisions and acceptance criteria below describe what to build.

## 1. Executive summary

AgenEditor transforms user-supplied raw video footage, optional B-roll, music, and instructions into a reviewable, publishable video. The first workflow targets a **40-second vertical talking-head Reel** derived from a 5–20-minute source video. An external AI agent interprets the creative brief and proposes a source-linked edit; AgenEditor validates that proposal, executes non-destructive edits, renders a preview, runs technical QA, and supports user-requested revisions before final export.

AgenEditor has **one core editing engine with two control surfaces**:
1. A native desktop app for asset management, reviewing timeline decisions, previewing and exporting.
2. An MCP tool server for Codex, Claude Code, and other compatible hosts.

The UI and MCP bridge **must share the same project model, service layer, permissions, version checks and render worker**. A model is never authorized to write arbitrary commands or edit arbitrary files.

### Non-negotiable principles
- **Editor only:** use user-approved original assets and derived proxies. Transcripts, rendered captions, edits and thumbnails are allowed; synthetic media is not.
- **Non-destructive:** original media never changes; each timeline edit creates an immutable revision.
- **Auditable:** every source range, caption word and B-roll overlay identifies the originating asset and time range.
- **Local-first:** media ingestion, transcription, proxy generation and rendering occur locally by default. Cloud model access is optional and explicitly disclosed.
- **Human-gated finalization:** a draft can be autonomous; final client delivery requires user approval for the MVP.
- **Provider-independent:** Codex/Claude Code are supported MCP clients, not dependencies of the core editor.

## 2. Product requirements

### 2.1 Target users and first use case
- Freelance video editors, social content teams, podcast producers and creators.
- Initial format: one-person talking-head clips, podcast highlights and similar interview footage.
- Input: 5–20 minutes of primary footage; optional user-supplied B-roll, music, logos, and SRT.
- Output: a **40-second target**, 9:16, 1080×1920, 30 fps H.264/AAC MP4 plus SRT, project and QA report.
- If the source cannot supply a coherent 40 seconds, report a constraint instead of fabricating dialogue or padding misleadingly.

### 2.2 Primary user stories
| ID | Story | Acceptance criterion |
|---|---|---|
| US-01 | Import a local project with media | Files are inspected, hashed, registered and remain unchanged |
| US-02 | Describe an editing goal | Brief is preserved and associated with a project revision |
| US-03 | Request an autonomous first cut | Agent selects real, valid source ranges forming one coherent idea |
| US-04 | Generate accurate subtitles | Words derive from the media transcript; timing maps to the final cut |
| US-05 | Use supplied B-roll and music | Only explicitly registered assets appear in the output |
| US-06 | Preview draft before delivery | User can play a rendered proxy and inspect the edit decision list |
| US-07 | Request a revision in natural language | Changes create a new version; old versions remain reversible |
| US-08 | Export a final video | Final video meets technical QA, stores immutable version provenance |
| US-09 | Work through Codex/Claude Code | Both can discover MCP tools, inspect projects, create edits and check jobs |
| US-10 | Work without cloud upload by default | Raw media does not leave the machine without affirmative permission |

### 2.3 MVP feature scope
**Included in first desktop MVP:**
- Local projects and source asset import; MP4/MOV/MKV input where FFmpeg decoding is supported.
- FFprobe metadata, thumbnail strips, waveform peaks and low-resolution proxy generation.
- Local transcription with faster-whisper; word timestamps and silence candidates.
- AI-assisted transcript-based hook/segment selection with human review and real source evidence.
- A structured, non-destructive cut timeline supporting V1 speaker, V2 supplied B-roll, A1 dialogue, A2 supplied music, T1 captions.
- Basic hard cuts, vertical crop/reframe controls, simple punch-ins, caption styles, audio fades/ducking and loudness adjustments.
- Preview render, cancel/retry job, progress visibility, versioned revisions and final 1080×1920 export.
- MCP project, asset, analysis, timeline, render, revision and QA tools.
- Desktop UI for importing, reading a cut list, previewing video, making basic corrections and exporting.

### 3.1 Asset preparation (external generation)

*Amended 2026-11-12 at the owner's request.* The agent workflow is **Plan → Prepare assets → Execute → Review**:

| Step | Who | What |
|---|---|---|
| Plan | Claude Opus 5.5 (high effort) | Source-cited edit decision list **plus** an `asset_requests` JSON block: one entry per storyboard frame or B-roll shot that the footage lacks (`id`, `kind` image/video, `purpose`, `prompt`, `aspect`). |
| Prepare assets | External tools, run by the user | Image requests go to ChatGPT by default, to Gemini if ChatGPT is out of quota; video requests go to Google Flow (MCP when a connector exists, otherwise copy-paste). AgenEditor shows a one-click checklist with "Copy for ChatGPT / Gemini / Flow" per request and a "Generate storyboard" entry. |
| Gate | AgenEditor | Execute stays locked until every request is imported and marked ready (or explicitly dropped). |
| Execute | Claude Sonnet 5.5 (high effort) | Carries out the EDL through MCP tools, using only registered assets. |
| Review | Claude Opus 5.5 (high effort) | Checks the cut and measured QA against the brief; sends notes back to Execute. |

In the desktop app (amended 2026-11-15) the user picks **Plan**, **Execute** or **Review** above the prompt before
each Claude run; the shell passes that stage's model and effort to Claude Code (`--model`, `--effort high`). A new
project starts on Plan, and after each successful run the picker moves on (Plan → Execute → Review → Execute); the
user can change it at any time. All stages share one conversation, so Execute sees the plan and the review notes.
Plan and Review cannot change the edit: the shell disables the engine's editing tools for them (Plan also cannot
render; Review may render a preview and run QA). With an empty prompt, Execute and Review use a default request.

Rules: AgenEditor makes no generation API calls and holds no generation credentials. Imported generated files are
registered like any asset (hash, probe, source-linked IDs) and carry provenance `generated-external` with the tool
name, shown as **AI-generated (external)** in the bin, plan and export QA report. Prompts sent to external tools
contain the brief and shot description only — no transcript beyond what the user approves, no local paths.

### 3.2 Sound library (added 2026-11-15)

Packs come from two places (amended 2026-11-15):

* **Free catalog (CC0).** A fixed list of Kenney packs published on OpenGameArt under CC0. *Interface Sounds* ships
  inside the installer and is installed (active) the first time the sound library opens; removing it keeps it
  removed. The other packs install only when the user clicks **Download & install**. The engine downloads from the
  entry's fixed HTTPS URL (host allow-list `opengameart.org`, redirects included), caps the size, and installs only
  if the bytes match the pinned SHA-256; otherwise nothing is installed. The editor agent has no tool that installs
  or downloads packs. This is the only stock media AgenEditor fetches.
* **Own folder.** The user installs a pack from a local folder they already downloaded (for example Pixabay or
  Mixkit sets).

AgenEditor copies, probes, hashes and write-protects each audio-only file (60 s or shorter, up
to 500 per pack) into `<workspace>/_sound_library/`, and records the licence the user states (CC0, royalty-free,
CC BY with a required credit line, or other). For folder installs AgenEditor does not verify the licence.

Each pack has an **Active** tick box. The editor agent can search only active packs (`list_sound_effects`) and
add a sound with `add_sound_effect`, which registers it in the project as role `sfx` with provenance
`sound-library` (pack, sound, licence, credit). Sound effects are placed on track **A3**; A3 clips may overlap,
are not ducked, and are limited to 100 per timeline. Uninstalling a pack leaves copies already registered in
projects untouched. The agent only adds sound effects when the user asks for them and reports any credit line.

### 3.3 Transitions (added 2026-11-15)

Transitions are built in: the 58 transitions of the bundled FFmpeg `xfade` filter, given friendly preset IDs and
grouped into four styles — **Classic** (dissolves, dips, wipes), **Modern** (slides, smooth wipes, covers,
reveals, squeezes), **Montage** (zooms, slices, wind, pixelize, diagonals, corner wipes) and **Cinematic** (slow
fades, blur dissolve, grey fade, iris and bar reveals). Nothing is downloaded or installed. The user ticks which
styles are active (workspace-wide, all active by default); `list_transitions` returns presets from active styles
only, and an agent `commit_timeline` that adds a transition from an inactive style is refused.

A timeline's `transitions` list holds `{after_clip_id, preset, duration_frames (2–60), rationale}` for cuts
between V1 clips; other cuts stay hard cuts. A transition never changes the total length: half of it comes from
just past the outgoing clip and half from just before the incoming clip (real source handles when available,
otherwise a held frame). Dialogue audio keeps its hard cut with edge fades, so speech timing and captions do not
move. Patches drop transitions whose cut no longer exists; edit plans start without transitions.

**Out of scope:** in-app generation of images/video/music/voices, multicamera editing, advanced motion graphics, full NLE-style realtime frame-accurate playback, collaborative workspaces, subscriptions, stock-asset search, cloud media hosting, timeline interop guarantees with Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve.

## 3. Final technology decisions

| Subsystem | Chosen stack | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop shell | Tauri 2 / Rust | OS integration, installers, native security permissions, packaged sidecars |
| Desktop UI | React + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind CSS | Strong ecosystem for asset panels, chat, inspector and visual timeline |
| State | TanStack Query + Zustand | Async commands versus local UI state; optional until app work begins |
| Engine | Python 3.12+ | AI/video analysis ecosystem and rapid typed service development |
| Agent interface | Official MCP Python SDK v2, stdio | Agent-neutral typed editing tools; supports Codex/Claude Code |
| Video processing | FFmpeg / FFprobe | Repeatable transforms, transcodes, composites and output inspection |
| Media indexing | PyAV + PySceneDetect | Video sampling, shot boundaries and thumbnail extraction |
| Speech | faster-whisper; WhisperX as optional later module | Local transcript, word-level timing and optional forced alignment |
| Contracts | Pydantic 2 + JSON Schema | Parse, validate and version source-linked edit plans |
| Persistence | SQLite (WAL) + project directories | Transactional job/revision tracking on a single user machine |
| Test/quality | pytest, Ruff, Vitest, Playwright, golden-media fixtures | Engine, agent adapter and UI correctness |
| Later NLE upgrade | Evaluate MLT; use OpenTimelineIO for interchange | Avoid forcing a real-time nonlinear editor into MVP |

**Alternative considered:** Qt/PySide6 offers native multimedia widgets and a single-language app, but it is not required for the initially preview-rendered experience. If direct realtime source-timeline playback becomes a dominant feature, prototype a dedicated MLT/Qt/native preview pipeline rather than assume browser-video playback is frame accurate.

## 4. Component architecture

```text
                 ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                 │ Desktop UI: Tauri/React     │
                 │ assets • review • export    │
                 └──────────────┬──────────────┘
                                │ typed desktop IPC
  ┌─────────────────────┐       ▼
  │ Codex / Claude Code │ ┌──────────────────────┐
  └──────────┬──────────┘ │ App IPC adapter      │
             │ MCP stdio  └───────────┬──────────┘
             ▼                       │
  ┌─────────────────────┐             │
  │ MCP adapter / bridge│─────────────┤
  └─────────────────────┘             ▼
                        ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                        │ Shared Engine Service Layer │
                        │ project / asset / analysis  │
                        │ edit plan / timeline / jobs │
                        └───────┬───────────┬─────────┘
                                │           │
                              SQLite    Render/AI workers
                                │           │
                                ▼           ▼
                         project store  FFmpeg/Whisper
```

### 4.1 Process model
1. **M1 headless development:** `ageneditor-mcp` launches with stdio and calls the engine package directly. No desktop application is required.
2. **Desktop integration:** Tauri launches a **packaged Python engine sidecar**. For robust shared state, use a **single per-user local engine service** with an authenticated local IPC endpoint (OS named pipe or a loopback-only endpoint with ephemeral token). The MCP bridge connects to the same engine rather than starting a competing render process.
3. **Worker isolation:** render and transcription run as managed child processes with explicit job IDs, progress, cancellation and crash reporting. A single render concurrency limit is adequate for v1.
4. **MCP stdio:** stdout carries protocol messages only; logs go to stderr / rotating files.
5. **Edits:** `expected_revision` / optimistic locking prevents desktop edits and MCP edits from silently overwriting each other.
6. **Shutdown:** pending work and state are persisted. Clearly report when a running render will cancel on shutdown; background rendering after app exit is deferred until supported by a dedicated worker lifecycle.

### 4.2 Service modules
- `project_service`: create/open/list/backup projects; manage workspace authorization.
- `asset_service`: ingest, hash, probe, thumbnail, proxy and immutable source registry.
- `transcript_service`: VAD, transcription, word timestamps, correction records.
- `scene_service`: shot segmentation and available B-roll metadata.
- `planner_service`: request typed proposed source ranges from an external AI agent; never accept hallucinated asset references.
- `timeline_service`: validate, commit, diff, undo and version edits.
- `render_service`: compile validated timelines to trusted FFmpeg argument arrays.
- `job_service`: durable render/transcription jobs, progress and cancellation.
- `qa_service`: technical checks plus editorial review warnings.
- `mcp_adapter`: expose typed tools; no editing business logic inside handlers.
- `desktop_adapter`: typed Tauri/Rust–Python IPC; same shared core services.

## 5. Data model and editing contracts

### 5.1 Project state
SQLite tables (minimum):
- `projects(id, name, root, created_at, updated_at, current_revision)`
- `assets(id, project_id, relative_path, sha256, kind, duration_frames, fps_num, fps_den, metadata_json)`
- `transcripts(id, asset_id, model, language, words_json, confidence_json, created_at)`
- `timeline_versions(id, project_id, revision, parent_revision, timeline_json, created_at, provenance_json)`
- `jobs(id, project_id, kind, status, version, progress, error_json, output_path, started_at, ended_at)`
- `qa_reports(id, job_id, results_json, created_at)`
- `agent_events(id, project_id, action, redacted_args_json, result_json, timestamp)`

Assets stored in project-scoped `originals/`, `proxies/`, `thumbnails/`, `transcripts/`, `timelines/`, `renders/` and `reports/` directories. Project DB must stay on a local filesystem when using SQLite WAL.

### 5.2 Canonical timeline
- Store times using rational frame rates and integer frame indices for frame-aligned video; audio tracks use sample-aware timing.
- Render profile records width, height, frame rate, pixel format and codec preset.
- Each clip has: immutable `clip_id`, `asset_id`, `source_in_frames`, `source_out_frames`, `timeline_in_frames`, `track`, `fit_mode`, transform and effect parameters.
- Audio overlays use source ranges plus gain/ducking envelopes.
- Captions are derived from exact transcript word IDs and mapped to output time; corrections are explicitly versioned.
- Every timeline has `schema_version`, `project_id`, `revision`, `parent_revision`, `target_duration_frames`, `render_profile` and `provenance`.
- Timeline renderer takes validated data only: agent-supplied shell commands or FFmpeg filter strings are forbidden.

**Illustrative minimal shape:**

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "project_id": "reel_001",
  "expected_revision": 3,
  "output": {"width": 1080, "height": 1920, "fps_num": 30, "fps_den": 1},
  "primary_cuts": [
    {"asset_id": "speaker_01", "source_in_frames": 360, "source_out_frames": 510},
    {"asset_id": "speaker_01", "source_in_frames": 1350, "source_out_frames": 1800},
    {"asset_id": "speaker_01", "source_in_frames": 2760, "source_out_frames": 3360}
  ],
  "caption_preset": "clean_white",
  "audio_preset": "dialogue_priority",
  "target_duration_frames": 1200
}
```

This example totals 150 + 450 + 600 = **1200 frames / 40 seconds at 30 fps**. Assume source timestamps in the specified timebase correspond to real material; this sample is not footage-derived. In production, VFR sources and timestamp normalization require canonical source timestamp mapping before frame conversions.

### 5.3 Source integrity
- Copy/import into immutable originals or maintain a controlled read-only reference with hash checks; choose copying as the default MVP path.
- Source ranges must exist within probed media duration and obey stream-type requirements.
- Export as new version to a temp file, verify it, then atomically publish.
- All revisions reference stable asset IDs, not guessed filenames.

## 6. MCP API specification

Initial tool contracts (JSON-serializable typed inputs and outputs):

| Tool | Key input | Key output |
|---|---|---|
| `create_project` | name | project ID, allowed import location |
| `register_asset` | project ID, path **relative to project imports** | asset ID, hash, metadata |
| `inspect_asset` | project ID, asset ID | codecs, streams, resolution, timestamps |
| `transcribe_asset` | asset ID, model preset | job ID; resulting transcript ID |
| `get_transcript` | transcript ID, optional range | timestamped words and confidence |
| `list_assets` | project ID | safe asset references and status |
| `submit_edit_plan` | project ID, structured agent-authored candidate, expected revision | source-grounded proposed segments, validation results |
| `validate_timeline` | candidate timeline | structural and semantic errors/warnings |
| `commit_timeline` | candidate, expected revision | immutable version ID or conflict error |
| `start_preview_render` | project ID, version | durable job ID |
| `get_job_status` | job ID | status, progress, warnings, output reference |
| `run_qa` | completed render job ID | pass/fail and review warnings |
| `apply_revision` | version, structured patch, expected revision | new version, diff |
| `export_final` | approved version, export preset | final render job ID |

**MVP minimum:** M1 implements create/register/inspect/validate/commit/render/status/QA. Transcription, semantic planning, revision and export-specific options arrive in later milestones.

**Tool policy:** tools never accept unrestricted directories, shell commands, network URLs or executable filter expressions. Return structured errors such as `ASSET_NOT_FOUND`, `RANGE_OUT_OF_BOUNDS`, `REVISION_CONFLICT`, `SOURCE_CHANGED`, `UNSUPPORTED_CODEC`, `RENDER_FAILED`, `QA_FAILED`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`.

## 7. Autonomous 40-second editing pipeline

1. **Ingest:** inspect original media with FFprobe, verify streams, hash asset, generate thumbnails/proxies and optional audio waveform.
2. **Analyze:** run local faster-whisper with VAD, get word timestamps, detect silence candidates and scene changes. Retain original source time offsets.
3. **Understand:** agent examines transcript and brief, identifies a single idea, proposes 2–5 coherent candidate segments and an appropriate opening hook. It must cite source word IDs/time ranges.
4. **Rank/select:** evaluate relevance, continuity, hook strength, context integrity and target length. Avoid misleading sentence stitching or inventing claims.
5. **Plan:** create an ordered edit decision list; prefer contiguous coherent passages when possible. Add limited B-roll from supplied assets only, mapped to relevant lines.
6. **Validate:** confirm media IDs, durations, no forbidden media generation, no missing audio, caption provenance and feasible output.
7. **Compile timeline:** build video, audio, B-roll and caption tracks; calculate exact frame/sample mapping and fades.
8. **Preview render:** FFmpeg creates compressed 720×1280 or configurable proxy; keep source and timeline unchanged.
9. **Technical QA:** decodeability, resolution, timestamps, black/silent sections, audio levels, caption bounds, track coverage and source checksum.
10. **Editorial review:** present warnings for awkward joins, uncertain caption words and crop risks. Show edit reasons and direct source locations.
11. **User revision:** natural-language request translates into a bounded typed patch, creates a new timeline revision and rerenders affected output. Only valid new revisions may be committed.
12. **Finalization:** require user approval; render 1080×1920 30 fps H.264/AAC, rerun QA and produce MP4/SRT/JSON/QA package.

**Failure rule:** if there is no suitable 40-second coherent selection or required audio is unusable, report it and offer a shorter edit, a different region or manual review. No invented timestamps, quotes or media.

## 8. Desktop UX specification

### Application screens
1. **Project library** — create, open, recent projects, disk usage.
2. **Editing workspace** — three columns: asset bin (left), preview and transcript/cut list (center), brief/agent activity and edit inspector (right); timeline strip along bottom.
3. **Agent handoff panel** — creative brief with **Copy to Codex/Claude Code** action, MCP connection instructions/status, progress stages, source justifications and warnings. Do not present a functional built-in AI chat in the MVP.
4. **Review mode** — preview player, source comparison, caption corrections, change history, approve/reject.
5. **Export** — aspect/resolution/preset, destination, QA report and finished file location.
6. **Settings** — FFmpeg/model availability, GPU/CPU mode, local-storage controls, data-sharing permissions and MCP connection help.

### Initial interaction design
- Drag/drop input is supported, but all imported sources become registered project assets.
- The visible timeline is a **reviewable/editable cut list** and proxy-based timeline strip, not an unsupported promise of full real-time NLE playback.
- Simple edit actions: reorder, trim, remove segment, toggle B-roll, change caption preset, lower music, undo/revert.
- The agent activity pane must show MCP actions and warnings, not unsupported assertions like “perfect edit.” Natural-language edit/revision instructions are sent through the external Codex/Claude Code host in the MVP; built-in model chat is deferred.
- A timeline version being rendered remains immutable. New changes create another version.

## 9. Worker, performance and hardware strategy

- Start with CPU rendering for broad compatibility, then enable tested hardware acceleration (NVENC, Quick Sync, AMF) via capability detection.
- Transcription supports CPU as fallback and optional CUDA acceleration where dependencies are correctly installed.
- Cache transcriptions by content hash + model/version/options, frames/scenes by asset hash, and previews by timeline hash + preset.
- Limit initial concurrency to one heavy render and one transcription to avoid resource spikes; make configurable later.
- Keep previews lower resolution; final export high quality using the same source-linked edit plan.
- Avoid imposing unverified runtime SLAs. Measure real processing on reference machines and publish benchmark results before advertising speed.

## 10. Quality requirements

### Automated gates
| Check | Proposed gate |
|---|---|
| Media validity | Output fully decodes with no fatal errors |
| Format | H.264/AAC MP4, 1080×1920, 30fps final |
| Duration | 40 sec ± 0.25 sec for strict reference test; normal user projects may allow ± 2 sec or explicitly configurable tolerance |
| Source preservation | SHA-256 hashes of originals unchanged |
| Timeline integrity | Every clip maps to registered media/time ranges |
| Caption provenance | All rendered dialogue captions map to transcript/corrected words |
| Audio target | Configurable target (initial preset approx. -16 integrated LUFS) and true peak at/below -1 dBTP |
| No accidental gaps | Report unexplained black or silent gaps beyond configurable threshold |
| Crash safety | Interrupted jobs are marked failed/interrupted and recoverable |

### Human/editorial QA
- Hook is understandable within the opening seconds.
- Spoken meaning is preserved; no misleading out-of-context splice.
- Cut points do not clip phonemes or breaths unnaturally.
- Captions are legible on phone UI and accurate with names/terms manually checked when uncertain.
- B-roll is relevant, non-repetitive and not confusing.
- Speaker remains visible when B-roll is not justified.

### Evaluation data set
Create a consented benchmark set of **10–20 real talking-head recordings** with human reference edits and annotated problem cases. Measure word error rate, segment relevance, source-range validity, caption sync, edit acceptance rate, manual correction count and error rate. Subjective “polish” is evaluated by humans, not claimed from technical QA.

## 11. Safety, privacy, permissions and licensing

- The user chooses the project import/export folder. MCP is scoped to project-import paths and registered IDs.
- No agent tool allows arbitrary shell execution or process launching. FFmpeg arguments are constructed from trusted schemas with `shell=False`.
- Model-facing content is redacted/minimized. Transcripts and frame descriptions may still be sensitive; sending them to Codex/Claude-hosted models requires clear disclosure and opt-in where appropriate.
- Provide a **local processing** mode that avoids optional remote services; external AI clients may still call remote providers, so mark their data-transfer status separately.
- Store API credentials in OS credential storage if/when native model providers are supported.
- Use authenticated IPC; if loopback HTTP is chosen, bind only 127.0.0.1, use random port/token and restrict CORS/origins. Never expose unauthenticated editing endpoints on the LAN.
- Every write checks project ownership, revision and allowed destination. Prevent path traversal and symlink escapes.
- Track licenses for FFmpeg binaries/codec options, models/weights, Tauri, fonts and all bundled dependencies before distribution. FFmpeg licensing depends on build configuration, including LGPL/GPL components; review official FFmpeg guidance.
- Separate errors, traces and optional telemetry; no asset telemetry by default.

## 13. Dependencies and deferred choices

### Required for initial headless milestone
- Python 3.12+, uv, `mcp>=2,<3`, Pydantic 2, pytest, Ruff.
- FFmpeg + FFprobe accessible on the developer's machine.
- SQLite (Python standard library initially; SQLAlchemy optional once persistence complexity warrants it).

### Required for autonomous short-form edit
- faster-whisper, PySceneDetect; PyAV only if sampling frames needs richer control.
- Compatible external AI agent that can receive transcript/metadata and call MCP editing tools.

### Required when desktop integration begins
- Node.js, Tauri 2, Rust toolchain, React, TypeScript, Vite.
- Packaging solution for Python sidecar (evaluate PyInstaller vs Nuitka through reproducible Windows clean-machine tests).
- Build scripts that bundle a compatible FFmpeg binary and comply with license requirements.

### Decision gates
- **M1 gate:** FFmpeg output correct without any AI model.
- **M2 gate:** agent generates valid source-linked plans, no hallucinated source references.
- **M3 gate:** captions/B-roll/audio produce reviewable quality.
- **M4 gate:** desktop UI and MCP bridge both edit the **same** project without corruption.
- **M5 gate:** clean Windows installer, no developer tools required, privacy and licensing review complete.

## 14. MVP definition of done

A fresh Windows machine with supported hardware can install AgenEditor, import a real 5–20-minute talking-head recording, optionally add preexisting B-roll/music, ask a supported external AI agent to produce a 40-second Reel, view a clear source-linked cut plan, generate a preview, make one natural-language revision, approve and export a working 1080×1920 MP4 with captions and an inspectable QA report. Originals remain unchanged. A technical failure is reported and does not masquerade as a successful export.
